html:
The Coree were a small Native American people of the coast of North Carolina, living south of the Neuse River in today's Carteret and Craven counties. Their language is not known; they may have spoken an Algonquian or an Iroquoian tongue.

Their neighbours included the Pamlico and Secotan to the north. Colonists fought them in a war around 1703, and in the Tuscarora War of 1711 to 1715 they fought on the side of the Tuscarora. After the defeat their survivors were absorbed into other peoples, mainly the Tuscarora. Core Sound and Core Banks are named after them.
